johannschopplich.copilot.agents.mcpUrl.h: Add this URL to your agent as a custom connector or remote MCP server. The agent then asks you to log in here.
johannschopplich.copilot.agents.setup.in: Kirby builds the MCP URL with http:// while the Panel runs on https://, and agents connect only over HTTPS. Set the url option in config.php to your https:// address.
johannschopplich.copilot.agents.setup.un: Agents can’t reach the MCP URL: {url} didn’t ask them to log in. A firewall, a security plugin, or a server rule may block POST requests to it. HTTP basic auth in front of the site stops agents, since they can’t answer its login prompt.
johannschopplich.copilot.agents.setup.au: Your server drops the Authorization header before it reaches Kirby, so agents can’t log in. On Apache, add SetEnvIf Authorization "(.+)" HTTP_AUTHORIZATION=$1 to the .htaccess, as in Kirby’s own. On nginx with PHP-FPM, add fastcgi_param HTTP_AUTHORIZATION $http_authorization;.
johannschopplich.copilot.agents.setup.we: Agents can’t load {url}. A server rule may block paths that start with a dot before they reach Kirby. Exempt /.well-known/ from it, as Kirby’s own .htaccess does.
johannschopplich.copilot.agents.setup.su: Agents can’t load {url}: Kirby runs in {folder}, so requests to the root of the domain never reach it. Add a server rule at the root of the domain that passes this URL to Kirby.
johannschopplich.copilot.agents.revoke.c: Revoke access for {agent} connected as {account}? It ends at once, and the agent has to connect again.
